questions.question: Dermatophytosis (ringworm): name two clinical types and give the treatment of each.

parts.text: What are two types of ringworm and what are their two treatments?

parts_raw.text: What are two types of ringworm and what is their two treatments?

questions.model_answer: a) Two types of ringworm with treatment: (1) Tinea corporis (ringworm of glabrous skin/trunk, most often Trichophyton rubrum) - small well-defined lesions: topical terbinafine or an imidazole (miconazole, econazole, clotrimazole); larger/widespread lesions: oral terbinafine 250 mg/day for 2 weeks (alternatives itraconazole 200 mg/day for 1 week, or fluconazole 250 mg weekly for 2-4 weeks). (2) Tinea pedis (athlete's foot, T. rubrum or T. interdigitale): interdigital disease topical terbinafine or an imidazole for 2-4 weeks; dry/moccasin type oral terbinafine 250 mg/day for 2-4 weeks (alternatives itraconazole 400 mg/day 1 week per month, or fluconazole 200 mg weekly for 4-8 weeks). Topical terbinafine can clear tinea pedis in 7 days.

cohort_answer.text: Tinea corporis, tinea pedis, tinea cruris, tinea capitis. Microsporum canis, M. gypseum, M. audouinii. Epidermophyton floccosum. Trichophyton rubrum, T. mentagrophytes, T. tonsurans, T. violaceum, T. verrocosum. Terbinafine: 250 mg per day for two weeks. Itraconazole: 200 mg twice daily for one week. Fluconazole: 150 mg once weekly for two to six weeks

questions.question: What is the molecular target of the following antifungals: posaconazole, micafungin, amphotericin, terbinafine?
questions.question_raw: PM 9. What is the molecular target of the following antifungals (4): Posaconazole, Micafungin, Amphotericin, Terbinafine

parts.text: State the molecular target of each antifungal.

parts_raw.text: State the molecular target of each antifungal

questions.model_answer: Posaconazole: lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase (Erg11/CYP51), blocking lanosterol-to-ergosterol conversion. Micafungin: 1,3-beta-D-glucan synthase (inhibits fungal cell wall glucan synthesis). Amphotericin: ergosterol in the fungal cell membrane — polyene binds ergosterol and forms pores, increasing permeability. Terbinafine: squalene epoxidase, an early enzyme in the ergosterol biosynthesis pathway.

cohort_answer.text: Posaconazole - 14-alpha demethylase inhibitor (stops lanosterol to ergosterol). Micafungin - 1,3-beta-glucan synthetase enzyme inhibitor (fungal cell wall). Amphotericin - polyene, binds irreversibly to ergosterol in fungal cell membrane, increases permeability. Terbinafine - Squalene oxidase/epoxidase inhibitor (early step in ergosterol pathway).

questions.model_answer: Posaconazole: lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase (Erg11/CYP51) — blocks ergosterol synthesis. Caspofungin: 1,3-beta-D-glucan synthase — inhibits fungal cell wall glucan synthesis. Terbinafine: squalene epoxidase — early ergosterol-pathway enzyme. Amphotericin: binds ergosterol in the fungal cell membrane, forming pores that increase permeability.

questions.question: [image-based question: picture of kerion (boggy scalp lesion), a T-cell-mediated hypersensitivity to the causative dermatophyte (Trichophyton and Microsporum spp.), presenting as a tender erythematous suppurative swelling with alopecia and regional lymphadenopathy].
questions.question_raw: [image-based question: picture of kerion (boggy scalp lesion), T-cell mediated hypersensitivity to causative dermatophyte (trichophyton and microsporum spp), tender erythematous suppurative swelling with alopecia and regional LAD]
questions.model_answer: a) A kerion is an inflammatory form of tinea capitis and requires systemic (oral) antifungal therapy; topical agents alone are inadequate. Treatment is directed by the causative organism: for Trichophyton infections, oral terbinafine (weight-based in children: <20 kg 62.5 mg/day, 20-40 kg 125 mg/day, >40 kg 250 mg/day) for about 2-4 weeks; for Microsporum infections, griseofulvin 10-20 mg/kg/day for a minimum of 6 weeks (Microsporum responds less well to terbinafine). Adjunctive measures: a topical azole cream/shampoo and removal of crusts with saline soaks; the pustules are usually not secondary bacterial infection, so antibiotics are not routinely required.

cohort_answer.text: Terbinafine 250mg PO daily x4-6 weeks (first line in Canada)
